title: The Agentic AI Engineer - Benedikt Sanftl, Mutagent

primary.label: AI Platforms & Developer Tooling
primary.rationale: The talk's primary focus is on agent loops (offline and online), multi-agent design with an orchestrator, and harness architecture for building AI agents through an eval-driven development loop. Mutagent is a developer platform for building AI agents that integrates with coding environments like Cursor and generates task definitions for coding agents. The talk explicitly maps the full agent lifecycle from spec through build, evaluate, ship, monitor, diagnose, and optimize across offline and online loops. Prerequisites include familiarity with agentic coding loops, agent frameworks, evaluation metrics, and observability platforms like LangFuse. This is a conference presentation with slides and a live demo of the diagnostics agent in research preview. summary: Bene and Burak from Mutagent present the Agentic AI Engineer, which applies agentic loops to building AI agents, mirroring coding agent loops for software. Two loops exist: an offline loop (spec, build, evaluate, improve) and an online loop (monitor traces, diagnose, feed back into optimization). The full lifecycle includes spec (define responsibilities, functions, decisions, context, tools, constraints), build (realize the spec platform-agnostically), evaluate (define evals and datasets analogous to unit tests), ship (deploy to production), monitor (continuous monitoring with trigger conditions), diagnose (collect failures, structured root cause analysis), optimize (create specific mutations for found failure modes), and repeat. Spec-driven development isolates requirements from implementation, enabling platform flexibility since frameworks change rapidly and hit bottlenecks. Eval-driven development is the TDD equivalent for agents, providing termination conditions. Evaluation must provide actionable feedback: binary criteria are preferred over score-based rubrics because failures give clear calls to action. LLM-as-judge solutions must be calibrated to handle scoring variance across runs, or experiments can't conclusively show improvement. After evaluation, production diagnostics collect learned failure modes grouped by root causes—agent prompt sections, missing or malfunctioning tools. Over time, agents accumulate code-checkable indicators per failure mode, enabling diagnosis without reading every trace, which matters because reading millions of traces costs more than execution itself. Representative sampling via intelligent segmentation becomes essential. Diagnostics produce a recursive why-chain for root causes, offer multi-choice remedies with an assumptions block for transparency, and generate a markdown task definition for coding agents to apply fixes. The Mutagent product runs in the user's environment (cloud and local) with a managed service planned. Two agents are in research preview: the evaluator agent (builds eval datasets) and the diagnostics agent (analyzes production traces). Both connect through an orchestrator running in the coding environment, with connectors to trace sources like LangFuse, ticketing systems, and Slack. The live demo shows the diagnostics agent retrieving traces, applying multi-tier filtering, and generating an HTML artifact summarizing detected failure modes, frequencies, root causes, remedies, and fix task definitions.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Introduction and Loop Concept
sections.summary: Bene (CEO) and Burak (CTO) introduce themselves and the concept of applying agentic loops to building AI agents. They define offline loops (build, test, evaluate, improve) and online loops (monitor, diagnose, feed back into optimization).

sections.title: Manual Loop Limitations
sections.summary: The manual lifecycle—implement change, generate samples, review traces, ship, AB test—is slow. Human review and build time become bottlenecks, especially when rolling out hundreds of agents. This motivates the Agentic AI Engineer as the natural next step.

sections.title: Agentic AI Engineer Lifecycle Stages
sections.summary: Burak walks through the full lifecycle: spec (define responsibilities, functions, decisions), build (realize spec in a framework), evaluate (define evals analogous to unit tests), ship (deploy to production), monitor (continuous monitoring with triggers), diagnose (collect failures, root cause analysis), optimize (create mutations for failure modes), then repeat the cycle.

sections.title: Cold Start vs Existing Features
sections.summary: Two entry paths: cold start (new agent from scratch, begins with spec/conceptualization) and existing features (optimizing an already-deployed agent).

sections.title: Spec-Driven Development
sections.summary: Spec-driven development captures agent requirements and success criteria. Key elements: context requirements, integrations/tools, jobs to be done (and not done), constraints and boundaries. The spec becomes a blueprint for future development.

sections.title: Build Stage and Platform Flexibility
sections.summary: The spec tells the coding agent what to build. Target platform choice remains flexible because the spec is isolated from implementation. This matters because frameworks change rapidly and can hit bottlenecks—new harnesses like Hermes and deep agents have emerged.

sections.title: Eval-Driven Development Loop
sections.summary: Eval-driven development is the TDD equivalent for agents, providing termination conditions. Evals consist of metrics/criteria and datasets. Initial eval suites come from domain experts or historical/synthesized data, but the real suite is a product of discovery from user feedback and production failures.

sections.title: Evaluator Agent and Evaluation Construction
sections.summary: Automated evaluator agents remove the human bottleneck of manually sifting through traces. Agent evaluation focuses on trajectory—context completeness, tool outputs in the trajectory, and harness effects on behavior. A useful eval goes beyond simple LLM-as-judge scoring to evaluate all vectors together.

sections.title: Actionable Evaluation Feedback and LLM-as-Judge Calibration
sections.summary: Evaluation must provide actionable feedback. Binary criteria are preferred over score-based rubrics because failures give clear calls to action. LLM-as-judge solutions must be calibrated to handle scoring variance between runs, or experiments cannot conclusively show improvement.

sections.title: Production Diagnostics and Learned Failure Modes
sections.summary: After going live, diagnostics collect primary signals and learned failures. Failure modes are identified, grouped by root causes (agent prompt sections, missing/malfunctioning tools), and used to generate new evaluations and remedies. Over time, agents accumulate code-checkable indicators per failure mode, reducing the need to deep-read traces.

sections.title: Trace Sampling and Autonomous Optimization Loop
sections.summary: Reading millions of traces costs more than execution itself, so diagnostics use intelligent segmentation and learned indicators to pick representative samples. The autonomous optimization loop runs experiments to reach target eval scores, and when the eval suite is green, changes ship automatically to production, where the online loop feeds failures back.

sections.title: Full Lifecycle Recap and Product Overview
sections.summary: Bene recaps the end-to-end loop: spec, build, offline evaluation/optimization, deploy, then online monitoring/diagnosis deriving new eval criteria into the spec. He introduces the Mutagent product: runs in user's environment (cloud and local), managed service planned. Two research-preview agents—evaluator and diagnostics—connect through an orchestrator in the coding environment with connectors to trace sources, ticketing systems, and Slack. Target platforms include GitHub PRs, MD file adjustments, and managed services.

sections.title: Live Demo: Diagnostics Agent
sections.summary: Burak demos the diagnostics agent triggered via a 'diagnose' command in a coding harness (Cursor). The orchestrator shows a dashboard of stages, agents, and prior configurations. Diagnostics retrieves traces from configured sources (LangFuse, local, JSONL), applies multi-tier filtering/segmentation for representative sampling, and generates an HTML artifact showing agent details, tools, framework, detected failure modes with frequencies, a recursive why-chain for root causes, multi-choice remedies with an assumptions block for transparency, and a final markdown task definition for coding agents to apply fixes. Users can also guide diagnostics toward specific reported issues. Bene closes by encouraging attendees to let agents handle tedious debugging work.

LLM-as-judge variance makes it hard to conclusively compare agent versions without calibration
